newsitem.title: UK: London precious metal prices sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: London precious metal prices sharply lower.

text.p: Precious metal prices were sharply lower across the board on Wednesday and dealers forecast further volatility in the platinum and palladium markets but saw the gold price trying to settle around present levels.

A rush of selling by the professionals in Tokyo's Tocom futures market wiped out an investor-driven limit up move and erased the gains made in platinum and palladium during the first two days of the week.
The Tocom palladium market rose by its daily limit five days in a row before the overnight oscillations.

The platinum group metals (PGMs) have been in turmoil for most of the year as Russia, the biggest supplier of palladium and second largest exporter of platinum, has been unable to deliver since last December due to administrative problems.
Dealers said the price moves were the outcome of thinking that as soon as Russia began delivering, prices would collapse.

"The vast majority are on the wrong side of the market. Only about 40 percent of the (Japanese investors) in palladium have covered their positions," a dealer said, indicating that further covering and volatility could be expected.
Platinum was indicated at $431.00/$436.00 per ounce about $16.00 and palladium was at $227.00/$231.00 down $7.50 after fixed at a new 17-year high of $245.50 on Tuesday.
Attempts to take gold higher succumbed to pressure from rampant dollar, stock and bond markets, low inflation expectations and no indication interest rates were likely to be hiked in the near future.
It was fixed at $318.85 down from $321.10 on Tuesday having encountered selling on New York's Comex futures market.
"I was surprised at the way the market turned. On the charts it looked like a good buy," one dealer said.
However after upward momentum began to ease late last week when produce selling stopped the price at around $227.00.
Key support levels at $324 and $321 fell this week dashing hopes that a floor had been established under the price.
"We have seen good physical interest this morning which we haven't had before this week so it could be beginning to bump along the bottom," one dealer said.
Silver was indicated at $4.34/$4.36 down three cents having seen profit taking after a try at $4.50 resistance failed.
"I expect to see it closer to $4.25 before the (Comex) option expiry on Friday," one dealer said.
